events.text: A runner in the white-and-blue of the Martial Alliance arrives with a summons: every Orthodox martial artist of Second-Rate or above is called to the Alliance headquarters. War with the Demonic Cult is coming.

effects.log: You kneel in the great hall with a thousand others. The Alliance Leader looks down at all of you and says nothing for a long time. Then: 'Some of you will not come home.'

choices.text: Send regrets: you are needed at home

effects.log: Your letter is polite. The Alliance files it under 'cowards', also politely.

events.text: The war between the Orthodox and the Demonic Cult has begun. Your company is ordered to hold the Iron Gate Pass for three days.

ok.log: Three days. Three nights. On the fourth morning the Cult withdraws, and the pass is still yours. Half your company is not.

fail.deathCause: the war at the Iron Gate Pass
fail.log: The pass falls on the second night. You are carried out under a pile of banners.

effects.log: You carry men down the mountain until your legs stop working. Some of them live because of you. They never forget your face.

events.text: The Martial Arts Tournament is held once a decade. Every sect sends its best. The winner's name is carved on the Dragon Stele for a hundred years.

ok.log: Five rounds. You win the final with your last ounce of strength. The crowd roars your name, and you hear it carved into stone as you sleep.

fail.log: You reach the last eight and lose to someone who will be a legend. People remember that you made them work for it.

effects.log: A hundred masters, a thousand techniques, one week. You go home with a head full of ideas.

events.text: The Seomun family announces a marriage-by-duel: whoever defeats their heir in a public bout may ask for the heir's hand. Half the young martial artists in the province have signed up.

ok.log: You win. The heir looks at you, then laughs, then offers you a cup of tea instead of a wedding. You become friends for life. The family is baffled.

fail.log: The heir disarms you in four moves and says, kindly, 'Come back when you mean it.'

effects.log: Thirty-one challengers. Thirty-one losses. The heir is still single, and extremely smug.

events.text: A master of the Unorthodox, famous for never losing, sends you a formal challenge to a life-and-death duel. Refusing will cost you your name in the murim. Accepting may cost you everything else.

ok.log: The duel lasts one breath. When the dust settles, the undefeated master is kneeling, and you have spared his life. The murim talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: He is everything they said. You survive only because he chooses to walk away.

ok.log: 'A life is not a wager,' you say, in front of everyone. Somehow, it makes you more respected, not less.

fail.log: They call you a coward in every teahouse for a decade.

events.text: You slip on a mountain path and fall into mist. You land, somehow alive, in a hidden valley. At the back of a cave sits a skeleton in a rotted robe, its bony hands resting on a stone box.

choices.text: Bow nine times before opening the box

effects.log: Inside: a manual, a jar of stone milk, and a note: 'To the one who bowed. Whoever did not bow found only poison.' You spend three years in the valley before you climb out.
A needle springs from the lock. You survive the poison, just, and find a manual under a false bottom. You suspect you missed something.

events.text: The old man who sweeps the sect's courtyard has swept around you for years. Today, he catches a falling roof tile with two fingers without looking up.

effects.log: A month of tea. Then one morning he says, 'Your breathing is wrong,' and fixes it in one sentence. Every morning after that, one sentence.

choices.text: Tell the elders what you saw

effects.log: When the elders come to look, he is gone. The courtyard is swept perfectly clean.

events.text: The sweeper is dying. He calls you to his tiny room and, with a shaking hand, points at the broom leaning in the corner.

effects.log: Inside the handle is a manual older than the sect itself. He was the last of a lineage everyone thought extinct. Now you are.

choices.text: Stay with him until the end

effects.log: You hold his hand until morning. He tells you his real name. It is in the history books. You never tell anyone.

events.text: A beggar with a knotted cord at his belt, the mark of the Beggars' Union, sits down next to you. 'Information, great hero. Fresh from every road in the land. Five taels.'

effects.log: Who is hunting whom, which sect is broke, which bridge is watched. The Beggars' Union knows everything, and today, so do you.
He eats three bowls and tells you the news for free. 'The Union remembers who feeds it,' he says.
The beggar shrugs. News is cheap, but not free.

events.text: You have offended a young heir of the Tang family, the masters of poison and hidden weapons. He smiles at you across the teahouse, and your tea smells faintly of almonds.

choices.text: Drink it and force the poison out

ok.log: You drink the whole cup, sweat the poison out through your fingertips and set the empty cup down. The Tang heir stops smiling. That night, he sends an apology and a jar of antidote.

fail.log: The poison is stronger than you are. You survive, but it will linger.

choices.text: Pour it on the floor and bow

effects.log: The floorboards hiss. The heir laughs and waves you off. 'Clever. Leave.'
You swallow the antidote, drink the tea, and ask for a second cup. The Tang heir is so impressed he forgets to be angry.
The poison goes through you like water through a sieve. You feel slightly warm. Everyone watching feels slightly afraid.

variants: You have offended a young heir of the Tang family, masters of poison and hidden weapons. He smiles at you across the teahouse. Your tea smells faintly of bitter almonds.

events.text: You wander into a bamboo forest and, an hour later, arrive back where you started. And again. The Jegal family is famous for its stone formations, and you are inside one.

ok.log: Stones, trees, the angle of the sun. You walk out on the third try. A Jegal elder is waiting, delighted. 'Nobody has done that in forty years. Stay for tea.'

fail.log: Two days of circles. A Jegal servant finally leads you out, trying not to laugh.

choices.text: Sit down and wait to be found

effects.log: A child from the Jegal family finds you by sunset and leads you out by the hand. It is humbling.

events.text: A proud Namgung swordsman overhears someone praising your swordsmanship. 'The Namgung are the first family of the sword,' he says, drawing. 'There is no second.'

ok.log: Nine exchanges. On the tenth, your blade rests against his collar. He sheathes his sword and bows. 'There is a second,' he admits.

fail.log: The Namgung sword is everything they say. He leaves you a cut on the sleeve and a lesson in humility.

choices.text: Agree that the Namgung are the first

effects.log: He looks disappointed, and leaves. You finish your tea in peace.

events.text: The chief of one of the Seventy-Two Greenwood Strongholds, the great bandit alliance, invites you to his mountain for wine. He wants you as a sworn brother. He also has two hundred men.

choices.text: Accept his table, refuse his brotherhood

ok.log: You out-talk him at his own table, over tea, and leave as a respected guest. Bandits in this province will leave you alone from now on.

fail.log: He takes the refusal badly. You leave by the cliff side, quickly.

effects.log: You swear under the black banner. You are now, technically, a bandit. The tea, to everyone's surprise, is excellent.
You send a polite letter. He sends back an impolite one. It rhymes.

events.text: The Golden Lion Escort Agency is hiring guards. Good pay, long roads, and bandits who are paid to not attack the agency's flag, mostly.

effects.log: A year on the roads. You learn every inn, every shortcut and which bandit chiefs can be reasoned with.
The agency's caravans pass you on the road with their lion banners flying. You wave.

events.text: Your caravan is carrying something the agency would not name, and tonight forty masked riders come for it.

ok.log: You hold the wagons until dawn. The cargo turns out to be a jade seal for the magistrate. The reward is enormous.

fail.deathCause: the night ambush on the escort road
fail.log: The cargo is lost. So, very nearly, are you.

choices.text: Lead the riders away from the caravan

ok.log: You lead forty riders on a chase through three valleys. The caravan escapes. The riders never find you.

fail.log: They catch you in the second valley. The caravan escapes anyway.

events.text: An official from the imperial court asks you to help arrest a martial artist accused of treason. The murim has an old rule: the court and the murim do not meddle in each other's affairs.

choices.text: Refuse: murim matters stay in the murim

effects.log: The official leaves stiffly. That night, every martial artist in the teahouse raises a cup to you.
The court pays well. The murim does not forget. Doors that were open start closing.

ok.log: He escapes the city an hour before the soldiers arrive. Years later, his sect sends you a gift every spring.

fail.log: The soldiers catch you both. You escape. He does not.

events.text: Bodies are found drained of blood in three provinces. The old men in the teahouses whisper a name nobody has said aloud for two hundred years: the Blood Cult.

effects.log: You follow the trail to a burned village. In the ashes: a red bone token carved with a closed eye. You keep it.
You decide it is only a rumour. More bodies are found in spring.

events.text: The red bone token grows warm in your pocket one night. It is pointing somewhere. Following it would mean walking into the Blood Cult's hands.

ok.log: It leads you to a hidden altar in an abandoned mine. You see their faces. One of them is an elder of the Orthodox Alliance.

fail.log: It was a trap. You escape the mine with burns on your arms and a single name overheard in the dark.

choices.text: Take the token to the Martial Alliance

effects.log: The Alliance thanks you and takes the token. A week later, the elder who received it is found dead. The token is gone, and you are certain now that the traitor sits in the Alliance's own hall.

events.text: The Blood Cult rises in the open at last. Its leader, the Crimson Patriarch, stands on the walls of a captured city and calls out every master in the land. You know his secrets. You are the only one who does.

choices.text: Name the traitor in the Alliance and lead the counterattack

ok.log: You name the traitor before the whole Alliance and lead the charge up the walls. The Crimson Patriarch falls. The murim will tell this story for a thousand years.

fail.log: You reach the Patriarch. You do not beat him. The Alliance wins the day behind you, but you are carried from the wall.

choices.text: Pass everything you know to the Alliance and fight in the ranks

effects.log: Your information wins the war. Someone else gets the glory. You find you do not mind much.

events.text: You return from a journey to find your master {npc} dead in the courtyard, a single black feather pinned to the chest. The sect says it was an illness. You know better.

effects.log: You burn incense before the coffin and make a promise out loud. Somewhere, someone hears about it and starts to worry.
The sect handles it. That is to say, nothing happens. The feather stays in your drawer for thirty years.

events.text: Years of searching end at a mountain monastery. The killer is an old monk now, pouring tea for pilgrims. He recognises you at once, and puts down the teapot.

ok.log: It is over quickly. Afterwards, you sit in the empty tea room for a long time. You expected to feel more.

fail.log: He is still terribly strong. He defeats you, then pours you tea. 'Your master was the better man,' he says. 'Go home.'

effects.log: He tells you why. It changes nothing about what he did, and everything about how you feel. You leave him to his tea and his guilt.

events.text: A courier from the Hushed Lantern Pavilion, the assassins' guild, offers you a contract: one merchant, one night, one thousand taels.

effects.log: It is done before the second watch. The money is real. So is the look in your reflection the next morning.
The courier bows and disappears. The merchant dies anyway, next month. Someone else took the job.
The merchant flees south and lives. The Hushed Lantern Pavilion adds a name to its list. Yours.

events.text: It has been years since you crossed the Hushed Lantern Pavilion. They have not forgotten. You notice the same beggar on three different streets in one day.

ok.log: You find their safehouse before they find you. The Pavilion decides, officially, that you are more trouble than you are worth.

fail.log: They were expecting you. You escape through a window with three needles in your back.

effects.log: A year in the mountains, alone. When you come back, the Pavilion has other problems.

events.text: Word has spread that you practise demonic arts. A band of Orthodox hunters has come to 'purify' you. Their leader is very polite about it.

ok.log: They leave with fewer members than they came with. The rumours about you grow darker.

fail.log: They were ready for demonic arts. You barely escape into the night.

ok.log: You are three provinces away before they reach your door.

fail.log: They catch you at the ford. You break free, bleeding.

choices.text: Seek refuge with the Demonic Cult

effects.log: The Cult opens its gates with a smile. It was only a matter of time, they say.

events.text: Under a blossoming plum tree, {npc} kneels, cuts {his} palm and holds out the knife. 'We were not born on the same day,' {he} says, 'but let us die on the same day.'

choices.text: Swear the oath of sworn siblings

mem.note: swore the oath of sworn siblings with me

effects.log: Blood, wine, three bows to heaven. From this day, {npc} is family.
'I will not promise to die on your day,' you say. 'I intend to save you from it.' {npc} laughs, a little hurt.

events.text: A stranger bumps into you in the market, and two fingers touch your side. You cannot move. Your acupoints have been sealed, and your purse is walking away.

choices.text: Break the seal with internal energy

ok.log: You force your energy through the sealed points. It hurts like fire. You catch the thief two streets later.

fail.log: You stand frozen in the market for two hours while children poke you. The seal wears off. The purse does not come back.

effects.log: Two hours of standing very still in a busy market. A pigeon sits on your head. Dignity is relative.

events.text: An auction house in the capital is selling a martial manual said to be the lost Ninefold Heaven Palm. Half the murim is here. Some of them are not here to bid.

ok.log: You win. On the way home, three different people try to rob you. The manual is real.

fail.log: You win, and it is a fake, though a good fake. You learn something from it anyway.

ok.log: You spot the three assassins in the crowd before the lights go out. You leave early. The auction does not end well.

fail.log: The lights go out. The manual disappears. So does a lot of the furniture.

events.text: {npc} is in closed-door training, and something is wrong: through the door you hear {him} screaming. {His} qi has turned against {him}.

choices.text: Break in and guide {his} qi with yours

ok.log: You press your palm to {his} back and fight {his} runaway energy until dawn. {npc} lives, and {his} meridians hold.

fail.log: The backlash throws you across the room. But you broke the cycle. {npc} lives.

mem.note: ran for help when my qi turned

effects.log: The healer arrives in time. Barely. {npc} walks with a limp, and holds no grudge.

events.text: A rumour sweeps the murim: an old master in the west has broken through to Harmony and grown young again, like a man of twenty. You look at your own grey hair.

effects.log: You find him. He looks twenty and talks like a grandfather. 'It is not the body that grows young,' he says. 'It is the qi. The body just follows.' You think about it for years.
If he can do it, so can you. You train until your grey hairs are the only thing that looks tired.

events.text: In the middle of practice, a faint blue light gathers along your blade and a leaf three steps away splits in two. Sword qi. You have reached the level where energy leaves the weapon.

effects.log: You practise until midnight just to see it again. From today, the murim will take you seriously.

events.text: The blue light on your blade thickens, hardens, and becomes solid: a sword aura, sharp enough to cut through steel as if it were water. Only true masters ever see this.

effects.log: You cut a boulder in half without touching it. Then you sit down, shaking, and laugh like a child.

events.text: The young genius of a rival sect requests a formal bout, with both sects watching. Losing would shame {sect}. Winning would make you famous.

ok.log: You win on the last exchange. Your sect erupts. The genius bows deeply and asks your name. You will meet again.

fail.log: You lose, honourably. Your sect is quiet on the way home. An elder says only: 'Again. Harder.'

choices.text: Propose a bout of form instead of force

ok.log: Two sword forms, performed side by side, judged by the elders. It is the most beautiful bout anyone can remember.

fail.log: The elders call it a draw, mostly to be polite.

events.text: On a moonlit bridge you meet a stranger who fights like the wind and laughs at everything. Only later do you learn this is the Heavenly Demon's own child.

effects.log: Letters hidden in hollow trees. Meetings on bridges at midnight. It is the most dangerous thing you have ever done, and the happiest.
You take the long way round for the rest of your life. Sometimes, on moonlit nights, you wonder.

events.text: War is coming between the Orthodox and the Cult, and your secret has been discovered. Both sides demand that you choose.

effects.log: You burn every letter. On the battlefield, across the lines, you see a figure standing very still. Neither of you raises a weapon.

choices.text: Choose love, and leave both worlds

effects.log: You vanish together into the southern mountains. The murim hunts you for a while, then forgets. You never regret it.

events.text: You wake from a dream of a life you have not lived yet. Faces, places, a death. By noon, the details fade, but one thing stays: you have done this before.

effects.log: From that day, you train like someone who knows how little time there is.

events.text: A child in the market has a face you know. In another life, that child grew up to kill you. Right now, the child is crying over a dropped rice cake.

choices.text: Buy the child a new rice cake

effects.log: The child beams at you. Maybe this time, things will be different. Maybe that is the point.

choices.text: Walk away and remember the face

effects.log: You memorise the face. This time, you will see it coming.

events.text: You remember, suddenly and clearly, that the bridge over the Yellow River collapses tomorrow. In your last life, you were on it.

ok.log: They close the bridge, grumbling. At noon, it falls into the river, empty. People start calling you a prophet.

fail.log: Nobody listens. You stand at the entrance all morning turning people away one by one. You save eleven.

effects.log: The bridge falls at noon. You were not on it this time. You try not to think about who was.

events.text: {npc} stops the lesson and stares at you. 'You already know this technique. How?' You cannot say that you learned it from your master, in another life, decades from now.

effects.log: Your master listens without laughing, then opens a scroll never shown to anyone. 'Then let us not waste this life.'
Your master's eyes narrow, then let it go. You train twice as hard to keep your secret.

events.text: The Heavenly Demon Cult comes down from the Hundred Thousand Mountains. City after city opens its gates. The murim holds its breath.

ok.log: The Cult's advance breaks at your city's walls. You were on those walls.

fail.log: The walls fall. You escape through the river gate with the refugees.

choices.text: Get civilians out of the city

effects.log: Nine hundred people, one secret mountain road. You go back for the last family three times.
You watch the smoke from a distant hill. The Cult does not come this far. This time.

events.text: At the top of the Crane Tower, where famous poets and martial heroes have left verses on the wall for five hundred years, there is one blank space left.

ok.log: You write eight lines about the river and the long road. By next year, children are reciting them.

fail.log: The tower keeper paints over it the following morning. Kindly.

choices.text: Leave the space for someone better

effects.log: You read every poem on the wall instead. It takes all day. It is worth it.

events.text: In a teahouse you meet a stranger with exactly the same murim nickname as you. The teahouse goes very quiet. The owner starts moving the furniture.

ok.log: You win. The stranger bows and agrees to be called something else. He chooses 'The Other One'. It catches on.

fail.log: He wins. For a year, people have to clarify which one of you they mean. It is humiliating.

choices.text: Share a pot of tea and compare notes

effects.log: It turns out you have both been blamed for each other's deeds for years. You split the bill and the reputation.

events.text: A beggar sells you 'the secret manual of the Heavenly Demon' for three copper coins. You open it. It is a recipe book.

effects.log: The braised pork is incredible. You decide the Heavenly Demon must have been a very happy man.

choices.text: Read it very, very carefully for hidden meaning

ok.log: It is a cipher. Every recipe is a breathing technique. The beggar is never seen again.

fail.log: It is a recipe book. It was always a recipe book. The dumplings are good though.
